reason: The sources support a surprising space story with over 10 verified multi-source claims about black holes and solar system orbital mechanics.
story: If the Sun suddenly turned into a black hole of the exact same mass, the Earth would not get sucked in. From far away, the external gravitational field of a black hole is identical to that of any other body of the same mass. While our solar system would get a lot colder because the black hole would not emit visible sunlight, our planet and the other planets would simply keep orbiting just as before, locked by gravity in their familiar paths.
angle: If the Sun became a black hole, Earth would keep orbiting it normally instead of getting sucked into a cosmic vacuum cleaner.

claims.claim: From far away, the external gravitational field of a black hole is identical to that of any other body of the same mass.
If you replaced the Sun with a black hole of the same mass, the planets would stay in their orbits.
Black holes do not act as cosmic vacuum cleaners and do not suck in other matter from afar.
A black hole is an astronomical body so compact that its gravity prevents anything, including light, from escaping.
The boundary of no escape around a black hole is called the event horizon.
Stellar black holes typically form as part of a supernova event when massive stars collapse at the end of their life cycle.
All black holes spin, and some rotate rapidly.
The supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way is called Sagittarius A*.
Sagittarius A* contains about 4 million to 4.3 million solar masses.

disputed: Whether the universe started from a singularity is unproved conjecture according to some physicists, while general relativity models point to it; scripts should attribute singularity origins as theoretical models.
